howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.threshold: an alarm opens an incident only if its severity is at least the one chosen in “Open incident from”; below the threshold it stays in the console without an incident.
howItWorks.grouping: later alarms attach to the incident already open for the same CI (or the same fingerprint); the open delay absorbs short spikes.
howItWorks.autoResolve: when the source resolves every alarm, the incident opened by monitoring is resolved; if the alarm comes back, it is reopened.
howItWorks.changeWindow: alarms on the CIs of a change in its release window are suppressed: no incident, no health change; at the end of the window they are re-evaluated.
howItWorks.flapping: an alarm that comes and goes too many times within the window is marked “flapping”: no incident opened or closed, CI health degraded, until it stays stable for the given minutes.
howItWorks.storm: if a source sends more new alarms per minute than the threshold, they are all grouped into a single storm incident instead of one per CI, until the rate stays below the threshold for the given minutes.

help.openIncidentFrom: Minimum severity from which an alarm opens an incident. “Never” = alarms stay in the console only.
help.groupBy: CI: one incident per CI, all its alarms attached. Fingerprint: one incident per distinct alarm.
help.openDelaySeconds: Seconds to wait before opening: if the alarm resolves within the delay, no incident. 0 = open immediately.
help.suppressUpstreamHops: How far up the dependency chain to look for a change in its window: 0 = only the alarm's CI; 1 = also a CI it directly depends on (e.g. a database being released silences alarms of the application that uses it).
help.flapThreshold: Above this number of firing/resolved transitions within the window the alarm is marked “flapping” and opens no new incident.
help.flapWindowMinutes: Observation window in which flapping transitions are counted.
help.retentionDays: Resolved events older than this many days are deleted.
help.matchShortHostname: If the alarm resource is an FQDN (db-01.example.local) also try the short name (db-01), and vice versa. Off: exact name or alias only. Beware of identical short names across environments.
help.autoResolve: When the source resolves every alarm of an incident opened by monitoring, the incident is resolved; a new alarm reopens it.
help.severityMap: Impact and urgency assigned to the automatically opened incident, from the alarm severity: the priority derives from them.
help.flapStableMinutes: How long the alarm must stay still (no new firing or resolved) before leaving the flapping state and returning to normal correlation.
help.stormThresholdPerMinute: When a source exceeds this number of new alarms per minute, a storm starts: its alarms are grouped into a single incident instead of opening one per CI. 0 = storm detection off.
help.stormCooldownMinutes: The storm ends once the rate stays below the threshold for this many minutes; later alarms return to normal correlation.

preset.valuesIntro: The tool sends severity and status in its own words: here you say what they mean for OpenGrafo. It applies before the connector's built-in table; a value that is neither translated nor in the vocabulary is rejected and shows up in the source's "Last error".

preset.defaultSeverityHint: In the tool's own words: it is translated like a received value (first the table above, then the built-in one). Empty = alarms without a severity are rejected (with the reason in "Last error").
preset.resourceIntro: An alarm without a host (aggregate metrics, Watchdog, log/APM monitors) cannot be linked to a CI: without a default resource it is rejected. Say here which object it belongs to.
preset.resourceHint: Empty = alarms without a resource are rejected (with the reason in "Last error").

preset.resourceFromAlertScopeHint: Applies before the default resource. Requires $ALERT_SCOPE in the Datadog custom payload.

hints.alertmanager: Alertmanager: the severity label is free text (page, critical, warning, none…); OpenGrafo already knows info / warning / critical. Status is always firing or resolved.
hints.grafana: Grafana: the severity label is free text; OpenGrafo already knows info / warning / critical. Status is always firing or resolved.
hints.zabbix: Zabbix: already known Not classified / Information → info, Warning / Average → warning, High / Disaster → critical; event_value 1 → active, 0 → cleared. Translate here to change the scale (e.g. Average → critical).
hints.datadog: Datadog: already known error → critical, warning → warning, info / success → info; transitions Triggered / Re-Triggered / Warn / Re-Warn / No Data / Re-No Data / Renotify → active, Recovered / Warn Recovered → cleared.
hints.dynatrace: Dynatrace: already known AVAILABILITY / ERROR → critical, PERFORMANCE / RESOURCE_CONTENTION / CUSTOM_ALERT → warning, MONITORING_UNAVAILABLE → info; State OPEN → active, RESOLVED → cleared.

grafana.step1: In Grafana open Alerting → Contact points → Add contact point and choose the integration "Webhook".
grafana.step3: Authorization header: scheme "Bearer", credentials: the token above.
grafana.step4: Make sure "Send resolved" is enabled, then attach the contact point to a notification policy.

zabbix.step1: In Zabbix open Alerts → Media types → Create media type, type "Webhook". The standard webhook media type is enough: no custom script is required.
zabbix.step2: Parameters: "URL" = the endpoint above, "Token" = the token above (sent as the Authorization: Bearer header), plus the fields below filled with the standard macros.
zabbix.step3: Fields OpenGrafo expects in the JSON body:
zabbix.step4: Create a user media with this type and an action that triggers it on problems and recoveries.

datadog.step1: In Datadog open Integrations → Webhooks → New, name it "opengrafo" and paste the endpoint above as URL.
datadog.step2: Custom headers: Authorization: Bearer with the token above.
datadog.step3: Payload: enable "Custom payload" and paste the template below, then mention @webhook-opengrafo in the monitors.

dynatrace.step1: In Dynatrace open Settings → Integration → Problem notifications → Add notification and choose "Custom integration".
dynatrace.step2: Webhook URL: paste the endpoint above. Add an HTTP header named "Authorization" whose value is "Bearer", a space and the token above.
dynatrace.step3: Custom payload: replace the template suggested by Dynatrace with the JSON below, as is. The placeholders go in quotes, except {ImpactedEntities}, which is already a JSON array.
dynatrace.step4: By default Dynatrace also sends the closing notification (State = RESOLVED), which lets OpenGrafo resolve the alarm: if your version shows an option for resolved-problem notifications, keep it enabled. Save and use "Send test notification" to verify.
